requirements.title: CLOSE STATUS values are KEEP or DELETE
requirements.definition: The STATUS= scalar-default-character-expression shall evaluate to KEEP or DELETE.

pending.close-status-keep-value: Close a named existing file with STATUS="KEEP" after writing known content and then read the content after reopening; this establishes KEEP as an accepted value.
pending.close-status-delete-value: Choose a controlled filename and first INQUIRE(FILE=,EXIST=) into a .true.-initialized logical to establish absence; OPEN it with STATUS="NEW", then INQUIRE(FILE=,EXIST=) into a .false.-initialized logical to establish existence before CLOSE(STATUS="DELETE"); after CLOSE, INQUIRE(FILE=,EXIST=) into a .true.-initialized logical and expect .false.
pending.close-status-other-values-prohibited: Source-control negative uses STATUS="UNKNOWN" on CLOSE and repairs only to KEEP or DELETE. This unnumbered shall is not a required diagnostic facet; any future observation must not require rejection unless a numbered owner is reached.

requirements.title: The STATUS specifier determines disposition of the connected file
requirements.definition: The STATUS= specifier determines the disposition of the file connected to the specified unit.

requirements.title: KEEP is not specified for a file whose prior status is SCRATCH
requirements.definition: KEEP shall not be specified for a file whose status before CLOSE execution is SCRATCH.

Because this is an unnumbered program restriction, the plan records no required processor diagnostic; a conforming positive control omits STATUS= and lets the scratch default be DELETE.

requirements.title: KEEP does not create a nonexistent file
requirements.definition: If KEEP is specified for a file that does not exist, the file will not exist after CLOSE execution.

pending.close-keep-nonexistent-file-remains-none: No portable oracle exists for this disposition effect because the required precondition, a unit connected to a file that does not exist while STATUS="KEEP" is allowed, cannot be established by standard Fortran: named OPEN with NEW or REPLACE creates an existing file, OLD requires an existing file, SCRATCH forbids KEEP and has no portable filename, and UNKNOWN status or external deletion would be processor-dependent or outside the program.

requirements.definition: If STATUS= is omitted, the default value is KEEP unless the file status before CLOSE execution is SCRATCH.

requirements.title: Omitted CLOSE STATUS defaults to DELETE for prior SCRATCH status
requirements.definition: If STATUS= is omitted for a file whose status before CLOSE execution is SCRATCH, the default value is DELETE.

pending.close-omitted-status-scratch-default-del: No portable oracle exists for the DELETE disposition of omitted STATUS on a SCRATCH file. A future source-control can open STATUS="SCRATCH", write known content, and CLOSE without STATUS=, but after CLOSE only unit disconnection is portable; the scratch file has no portable FILE= name for an EXIST= inquiry, so deletion itself cannot be verified by a single-image standard-conforming program.

Defines the role of STATUS= in file disposition.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.5.7-12.6.1, the CLOSE statement and data transfer statements in general (batch152). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds. Round 1 found a conditional KEEP-on-nonexistent-file plan and scratch DELETE plans that observed only unit closure; both are now explicit no-portable-oracle reasons (no portable way to connect a nonexistent file with KEEP allowed; no portable name for a scratch file), while named-file DELETE keeps a portable EXIST= plan established before the CLOSE. Round 2 found the nonexistent-unit CLOSE plan relied on OPENED=.false.; it is now guarded on INQUIRE EXIST=.false., since no unit number is guaranteed nonexistent. The eight numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
